text:
glen: Seeing autoscaler stuck when trying to scale gpu-a100-spot in us-west2. Pods Pending -> Reason=Insufficient IPs. cluster-autoscaler logs: "failed to allocate IPs: secondary range exhausted". Can infra triage?

ashwin: Which subnet/secondary range and what's the nodepool pod density? also which GPU SKU family (A100/A10/T4)?

glen: Subnet=redwood-gke-uswest2-subnet. Current pod secondary range gke-pods-west2 is a /22 (10.44.0.0/22). Nodepool gpu-a100-spot planned max=96 nodes, each node maxPods=30 (we use high pod density for batch), so worst-case ~2880 pod IPs. /22 size ~1024 IPs so we hit it. Accelerator quota for A100 shows Limit=96, Usage=88 -> need bump.

naomi: Short list of fixes: expand secondary range (replace with /20) or add a second secondary range and attach a new nodepool to it. Also open GCP quota increase for compute accelerators (A100) and possibly IN_USE_ADDRESSES for region. While support processes: limit maxPodsPerNode, move low-priority jobs to another region, or spin a temp nodepool in another subnet.

ashwin: Commands to inspect current state:
```
# show subnet ranges
gcloud compute networks subnets describe redwood-gke-uswest2-subnet --region=us-west2 --format="yaml(secondaryIpRanges)"
# region quotas for accelerators
gcloud compute regions describe us-west2 --format="yaml(quotas)" | grep -A4 accelerator
# pending pods
kubectl get pods -n batch -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending
```

glen: Ran the checks. Secondary range = 10.44.0.0/22. IN_USE_ADDRESSES for the subnet is at ~900. A100 quota = Limit 96, Usage 88. We want to request up to 320 to avoid repeated back-and-forth. Also note there are other clusters using the same subnet (staging/analytics) so we might need a clean plan to carve additional ranges.

naomi: I'll open the GCP quota ticket. Suggested request text for GCP support (paste to console):
"Project: redwood-prod, region: us-west2. Request increases: 1) Compute Engine Accelerators (nvidia-a100): from 96 to 320. 2) Increase subnetwork pod secondary range for redwood-gke-uswest2-subnet from /22 to /20 or add a second secondary range sized /20 (to provide ~4096 pod IPs). 3) Increase Regional IN_USE_ADDRESSES if needed. Justification: scheduled GPU-heavy training and batch inference campaigns requiring up to ~3k concurrent pod endpoints; business-critical workload. Contact: infra@redwood.ai."

cloud-provisioner: Opening quota request now. Created ticket Q-1B7M2Z-67890. Linking here. ETA from GCP: 4-72 hours depending on quotas requested.

ashwin: Thanks. Two operational notes while we wait: 1) carving a second secondary range is non-disruptive and fastest for a short-term relief; commands below. 2) verify CNI mode: if Calico is running in host-private-ip mode we could be consuming more node IPs than necessary.

ashwin: Example workflow to add a second secondary range and attach a nodepool to it:
```
# add a new secondary range to the subnet
gcloud compute networks subnets update redwood-gke-uswest2-subnet \
  --region=us-west2 --add-secondary-range=gke-pods-west2-2=10.44.16.0/20

# create a new nodepool using the new range (ip-aliases must be enabled on the cluster)
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-a100-extra --cluster=prod-gke-west2 --region=us-west2 \
  --num-nodes=4 --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100,count=1 \
  --enable-ip-alias --create-subnetwork=gke-pods-west2-2 --max-pods-per-node=24
```

glen: We'll gate today's scheduled training batch until quota or second-range is available. I flagged this as P0 for the schedule owners. Also please add @finance for cost approval if GCP asks about committed quotas.

naomi: Ticket Q-1B7M2Z-67890 updated with runbook and calendar for campaign. GCP support asked for project owner confirmation and business justification doc — attached.

ashwin: Quick mitigation suggestions for infra/schedulers while waiting:
- Reduce maxPodsPerNode on GPU pool to 16 to reduce immediate IP pressure.
- Evict non-critical pods from the affected nodepool and reschedule to other nodepools.
- Provision small cross-region pool (e.g., us-central1) for spillover (cheaper GPUs or preemptible).

glen: Also check kubelet --max-pods and ip-masq-agent settings. If ip-masq agent is off we might see pod network hairpin causing extra SNAT allocations.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3344 - "Pod IP exhaustion blocking GPU autoscale in us-west2". PagerDuty alerted.

naomi: We'll run a controlled test after quotas are increased: scale to +10 nodes, confirm pod IP allocation, check cluster-autoscaler logs, and monitor billing burn-rate for 24h. Leaving thread open until test passes. :white_check_mark:
